patch_description:
The strongest supplied policy preserved more particles and reevaluated memories. The current policy’s additional relocation and selective resets did not improve mean error, although these results do not isolate either mechanism’s effect.
This proposal allocates a displacement budget: observed deterioration increases exploration demand, while existing swarm spread and recent improvement reduce it. It jointly selects relocation fraction and radius, using fewer, wider probes when appropriate and preserving at least two of five particles. Memories are reevaluated and velocities retained. The hypothesis is that filling missing spatial coverage improves recovery without repeatedly disrupting useful search structure. Performance remains to be evaluated.
